The problem

Downloading is easy. The mess afterwards isn’t.

A browser download ends with a file on your disk. Everything after that — finding it, naming it, not downloading it twice — is left to you.

Files land in chaos

Videos, songs, installers and documents all pile into one Downloads folder with names like “videoplayback (3).mp4” — and stay there, unfindable, forever.

The same file, downloaded twice

Nothing warns you that you already grabbed that video last week. So the bandwidth, the time and the disk space get spent again — on a duplicate.

Interrupted means start over

A dropped connection, a closed laptop, a reboot — and a half-finished download is gone, along with every megabyte you already paid for.

How it works

Link in. Tidy file out. Three steps.

1

Paste a link — or just say it

Drop in a video, audio, file or torrent link, or tell the AI Assistant in plain words: এইটা ডাউনলোড করো Browsing instead? Hover any video and use the floating Download button.

2

Pick a quality — the real ones only

DOVIRA fetches the formats the site actually offers — video up to 2160p, audio as MP3, subtitles and thumbnails if you want them. If a video has no 1080p, DOVIRA won’t invent one.

3

It downloads — and tidies up

aria2 pulls it down over multiple connections, with pause / resume that survives restarts. The file gets a clean name, lands in the right folder, and duplicates are flagged before they waste bandwidth.

What it does

Fast downloads, without the mess afterwards

Most download managers stop at “downloaded.” DOVIRA keeps going — naming, sorting, deduplicating and resuming — powered by aria2 and yt-dlp under the hood.

AI Assistant — just say what you want

Paste a link and write a plain instruction — “download this in 720p” or “এইটা ডাউনলোড করো” — and DOVIRA starts it. When something fails, it explains why in plain language and suggests what to try next. Rule-based by default: no API key, no cost, nothing leaves your machine. An optional local model (Ollama / LM Studio) can step in for trickier cases.

English + বাংলা · Works offline

AI File Organizer

Downloads are sorted automatically into Video, Music, Documents, Archives, Programs, Images or Others — using the file type, video metadata and source site. Folder names and rules are yours to edit.

Smart filenames

Strips (Official Video), [HD], emoji and clutter from titles, then applies your template — like {title} [720p]. Preview it in the Add dialog, revert in one click.

Duplicate detection

Checks your history and destination folder for the same URL, same video + format, or same name + size — then offers Re-download, Skip, or Keep both before wasting bandwidth.

Floating Download button

The IDM-style button DOVIRA users asked for: hover any video on a page and a Download button appears right on it — one click sends it straight to the app. Works on Facebook Reels too.

Via browser extension

Browser extension, one-click pairing

Right-click “Download with DOVIRA,” toolbar popup, and optional download intercept. Pairing is painless: click Pair extension in the app, press Save on the page that opens — no copy-pasting tokens.

aria2 multi-connection speed

Direct files download over multiple connections via aria2, with pause / resume that survives restarts and reboots. Smart Download adapts connections to your real speed — more when it’s fast, gentler when it’s not.

Playlists, batch, clips, subtitles & torrents

Download a whole playlist or channel (pick the entries, one quality for all), paste many links at once, grab just a clip from a time range, save subtitles as .srt (including auto-captions), embed thumbnails and metadata — or open magnet links and .torrent files via aria2. Plus a site grabber that scans a page for downloadable files, a speed limiter, and a full history kept locally.

Install guide

Running in about a minute

Pick your system. On first launch, DOVIRA’s setup wizard walks you through your download folder, language (English / বাংলা) and the optional browser extension.

1

Download the installer

Get dovira-1.3.1-setup.exe from the v1.3.1 release on GitHub.

2

Run setup

Double-click the .exe and follow the NSIS installer. If SmartScreen asks, choose “More info → Run anyway” — the app is open source and unsigned.

3

Finish the wizard

Pick your download folder and language, optionally pair the browser extension, then paste your first link.

1

Download the .dmg

Get dovira-1.3.1.dmg from GitHub Releases and open it.

2

Drag to Applications

Drag DOVIRA into your Applications folder, like any Mac app.

3

First launch: right-click → Open

The dmg is unsigned (no paid Apple Developer account), so Gatekeeper blocks a normal double-click the first time. Right-click the app → Open — after that it opens normally. Terminal alternative: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/dovira.app

1

Pick your package

AppImage for any distro, or the .deb for Debian / Ubuntu — both on the v1.3.1 release page.

2

Make it runnable

AppImage: chmod +x dovira-*.AppImage then run it. Deb: sudo dpkg -i dovira_*_amd64.deb

3

Finish the wizard

Choose your download folder and language, and you’re ready to download.

New here? Follow these steps in order. You do not download the extension from the Chrome Web Store or from a separate link on GitHub — it comes with the DOVIRA app itself. You load that folder into Chrome once, then pair it with one click. DOVIRA needs to be installed first (see the Windows, macOS or Linux tab above), and it should be running while you pair.

1

Get the extension folder from the app

Open DOVIRA and go to Settings → Browser extension. That section holds the unpacked extension folder that ships with DOVIRA — and it gives you two ways to reach it. Click Copy folder path (the button is labelled in Bangla ফোল্ডারের পাথ কপি করো) and the app copies the path to that folder to your clipboard; or click Open folder (ফোল্ডার খোলো) to open the folder itself in File Explorer. Either way, remember that folder — in Step 4 you will select exactly it for Load unpacked. Don’t move, rename or edit the individual files inside it, and don’t pick a single file inside it when Chrome asks: you select the whole folder.

2

Open Chrome’s Extensions page

In Chrome, type chrome://extensions in the address bar and press Enter. (The same page is under Chrome’s menu → Extensions → Manage extensions.) This is the page where Chrome lists every extension installed in the browser.

3

Turn on Developer mode

On the Extensions page, switch on the Developer mode toggle in the top-right corner. Nothing is installed yet — turning this on simply reveals the extra buttons Chrome normally hides, including Load unpacked, which you need for the next step. Leave Developer mode on afterwards: Chrome requires it to keep an unpacked extension like this one installed.

4

Click “Load unpacked” and select the folder

Click Load unpacked. In the folder picker that opens, navigate to the extension folder from Step 1, click the folder itself once to select it, then confirm with Select Folder. Chrome loads it straight away and the DOVIRA extension appears in the list on the Extensions page. If Chrome shows an error, you almost certainly selected a file inside the folder, or the folder one level above or below it — go back and select the extension folder itself.

5

Click “Pair extension” in DOVIRA

Back in the DOVIRA app, stay in Settings → Browser extension and click Pair extension. The extension’s Options page opens in your browser with the connection details already filled in for you. There is nothing to copy and no token to paste — that is the point of the one-click pairing.

6

Press Save — done

On the Options page that just opened, press Save. That completes the pairing and the extension shows as paired. To try it, open a page with a video, hover over the video and use the floating Download button that appears on it, or right-click and choose “Download with DOVIRA.” If nothing happens, check that DOVIRA itself is running — the extension sends downloads to the app on your own machine.

Why Developer mode in Chrome? The Chrome Web Store prohibits YouTube-download extensions, so DOVIRA’s extension installs unpacked. It talks only to the app on your own machine (127.0.0.1, token-authenticated). Firefox users will get an AMO listing.

FAQ

Questions, answered honestly

Is DOVIRA really free?

Yes — completely. MIT licensed, no ads, no tracking, no account, and no pro-lock. Every feature is unlocked for everyone, forever. The source code is public on GitHub.

Why does fetching a video take about 10 seconds?

That’s normal — and it’s not DOVIRA being slow. Under the hood, yt-dlp has to ask the site for the video’s real format list, and that extraction takes about 9–13 seconds. Results are cached for 5 minutes, so opening the same video again is instant. In v1.3.1 the Add dialog itself opens instantly while formats load in the background.

Can it download YouTube videos?

Yes, via yt-dlp — Video up to 2160p or Audio as MP3, with subtitles and thumbnails if you want them. The quality list only shows formats the site actually offers for that video; if a video has no 1080p, DOVIRA won’t invent one.

Is my data sent anywhere?

No. Downloads, history and settings stay on your machine. The AI Assistant is rule-based by default, and the optional local model (Ollama / LM Studio) also runs entirely on your computer. The only network check is for app updates from GitHub Releases — which you can turn off in Settings.

How does the floating Download button work?

It comes with the browser extension. Once the extension is paired, hovering a video on a page shows a Download button right on the video — click it and the download starts in DOVIRA. Pairing is one-click: “Pair extension” in the app, then Save on the page that opens.

Why is the macOS version unsigned?

There’s no paid Apple Developer account behind this free project, so the .dmg can’t be signed. On first launch, right-click the app and choose Open (or clear quarantine in Terminal — see the Install guide). After that, it opens normally.

Can it download from Netflix or Prime Video?

No — and no download manager can. Those services are DRM-protected, and DOVIRA never tries to break DRM. You’re responsible for following each site’s terms and copyright law; torrents are supported for legal content like Linux ISOs and public-domain media, and DOVIRA never seeds after a download finishes.

What happens if a download is interrupted?

DOVIRA resumes it. Pause / resume survives app restarts, network drops and PC reboots — and if a partial file is genuinely gone, the app tells you instead of silently starting over.

Is v1.3.1 a stable release?

Not yet — all current releases are pre-releases. v1.3.1 is fully built and tested, and a stable release is the next step on the roadmap, after a final end-to-end check of extension pairing and clean installs.
